note: Curated New England solar / net-metering / REC market / regulatory updates for array operators. Each item is tagged with its state (or "region" for New England-wide, "rec" for REC-market-wide); the page filters to the reader's state. Refreshed by a research agent; verify against the linked source before relying on any figure.

items.title: November 2026 broker quotes put MA Class I RECs near $38/MWh; legacy SREC IIs still above $220
items.summary: As of November 2026, Sol Systems' Massachusetts REC schedule lists Class I certificates at about $38/MWh on a variable brokerage basis (and $29.50/MWh on a two-year fixed annuity), while legacy SREC II certificates are quoted around $221.75 each. The Class I level remains just under the $40/MWh Alternative Compliance Payment ceiling that MA, CT and RI now share.

items.title: Acadia Center: NECEC Quebec hydro lifts New England net imports to their highest since 2022
items.summary: An Acadia Center assessment (published Aug 26, 2026, updated Oct 26, 2026) finds the New England Clean Energy Connect line is adding Quebec hydro imports to regional supply rather than displacing existing Phase II exports: average net imports rose from 798 MW/hour in spring 2025 to 1,625 MW/hour in spring 2026, lifting imports to 13% of regional energy (up from 7%) and putting 2026 net imports on track for their highest level since 2022. NECEC had delivered about 3.9 TWh of its 9.55 TWh annual obligation as of mid-July; a second planned outage is scheduled Nov 5–17, 2026. The contracts require environmental attributes to be tracked under NEPOOL-GIS, and the hydro is expected to cover most Massachusetts Clean Energy Standard demand, leaving Class I certificates banked for Class I compliance.

items.title: Maine PUC unanimously denies CMP's $69.3M temporary distribution rate increase
items.summary: On October 6, 2026 the Maine Public Utilities Commission voted unanimously to deny Central Maine Power's roughly $69.3 million temporary distribution rate increase (about $7/month for a typical customer), with all three commissioners citing affordability and customer confusion and finding the entire temporary amount 'disputed.' CMP's larger ~$189 million permanent distribution rate case remains pending; Chair Phil Bartlett said a decision is most likely in April 2027 and signaled some increase is probable, though less than CMP requested.

items.title: Vermont PUC holds first Rule 5.100 net-metering rulemaking workshop, focused on distributed-solar grid impacts
items.summary: The Vermont Public Utility Commission held its first stakeholder workshop on October 2, 2026 at 9:30 a.m. in the rulemaking to update Commission Rule 5.100 (construction and operation of net-metering systems), which it opened by order on September 9, 2026. The session centered on the potential impacts of distributed solar on Vermont's transmission infrastructure; the rulemaking also implements Act 38 of 2025, which raised the expedited-registration threshold for ground-mounted systems from 15 kW to 25 kW.

items.title: Rooftop solar forces New England to rethink its grid as behind-the-meter PV nears 7,000 MW
items.summary: A Sept 23, 2026 Concord Monitor report notes New England now has roughly 7,000 MW of rooftop and other behind-the-meter solar — capable of producing over five times Seabrook Station's output on a sunny day, and roughly doubling in the last couple of years — after ISO New England logged its 500th 'duck curve' day on Sept 21, 2026 (the 107th of 2026 alone). Analysts say billing and payment mechanisms built for a one-way grid, including net metering, need to adapt to the steep evening ramps.

items.title: Massachusetts energy-affordability bill stays stalled in conference as Healey weighs winter relief
items.summary: As of late September 2026 the Massachusetts omnibus energy-affordability bill remained in a House-Senate conference committee (Barrett-Creem-Tarr) with no deal, prompting Gov. Maura Healey to say her administration is weighing direct relief for households heading into winter; negotiations were still ongoing in early November. The pending legislation would leave residential rooftop net metering intact while trimming net-metering credit values for larger non-residential facilities.

items.title: Connecticut standard-service rates keep falling as public-benefits bill credit runs through April 2027
items.summary: A Sept 17, 2026 CT Mirror report notes electricity prices are falling heading into the election: Eversource standard-service supply dropped to 11.577¢/kWh on July 1, 2026 and a public-benefits bill credit of roughly $30–34/month runs through April 2027, driven largely by long-term Millstone and Seabrook nuclear contracts. Eversource's pending PURA distribution rate case still seeks a double-digit increase for July 2027.

items.title: RI net-metering overhaul (Docket 26-30-EL) draws OER and Ameresco intervention as PUC reviews cap cut to 175 MW
items.summary: Rhode Island Energy's revised net-metering provision — filed Aug 14, 2026 (Docket 26-30-EL, proposed effective Sept 13, 2026) — lowers the aggregate ground-mount remote-net-metering cap from 275 MW to 175 MW, extends the qualifying-project deadline from July 1, 2030 to Dec 31, 2032, and adds an optional 25-year 'Fixed Renewable Net Metering Credit' of 19¢/kWh (escalating 2.75%/yr from 2028) for public, educational, hospital and nonprofit systems. The Office of Energy Resources (Sept 8) and Ameresco (Sept 16) filed to intervene; the PUC must approve an implementing tariff by Dec 1, 2026.

items.title: Power Advisory: New England basic service rates jump ~14% for 2H 2026, lifting net-metering payouts
items.summary: A Sept 14, 2026 Power Advisory report finds second-half 2026 basic/standard-service supply rates rose about 14% on average across six New England utilities year-over-year — roughly 14% in Massachusetts, 15% in Rhode Island, 25% in New Hampshire and 3% in Connecticut — driven by elevated gas prices, a harsh winter and NECEC underperformance. Because net-metering and community-solar compensation is linked to basic service rates, the analysis notes project owners will see higher payouts, with a further ~12% average increase projected for 1H 2027 (Eversource CT up ~25%).

items.title: Vermont PUC finalizes a 5.5% Green Mountain Power rate increase (Case 26-0096-TF), below the 7.5% requested
items.summary: The Vermont Public Utility Commission's Aug 28, 2026 order approved a 5.5% distribution rate increase for Green Mountain Power's 275,000+ customers — below the 7.5% the utility sought (Case 26-0096-TF) — effective Oct 1, 2026. Regulators approved about $113 million of 'resilience' infrastructure spending, roughly a third of GMP's $341 million request, citing affordability as central to the analysis.

items.title: Maine DOER proposes a Front-of-the-Meter DER program for renewables cut out of Net Energy Billing
items.summary: Maine's Department of Energy Resources published a draft Front-of-the-Meter Distributed Energy Resources (FTM DER) program proposal in late August 2026 — a successor pathway for larger renewable projects excluded from Net Energy Billing under LD 1777. DOER held a Sept 2 webinar, took written comments through Sept 11, and must submit a program design to the MPUC by Sept 30, 2026; the program would let projects contract with utilities and feed the standard offer.

items.title: Gov. Healey signs data-center executive order shielding ratepayers as omnibus energy bill stays in conference
items.summary: Governor Maura Healey signed an executive order on Sept 8, 2026 requiring new data centers to meet their power demand with clean energy, obtain local approval, and cover their own grid costs to protect ratepayers. Advocates urged it as a model for the stalled energy-affordability bill (S.3143 / H.5175), which remained in conference committee; that bill would leave residential rooftop net metering intact while trimming credits for large non-residential facilities.

items.title: Power Advisory: New England Class I RECs hold near the $40 ACP into a sixth undersupplied year
items.summary: An August 2026 Power Advisory update reports New England Class I RECs have traded close to the $40 Alternative Compliance Payment through a sixth straight undersupplied year, with forwards (Marex Spectron, as of Aug 13, 2026) still near the cap. Rhode Island has aligned its RES ACP to $40 flat, making the ceiling uniform across MA, CT and RI; separately, NECEC Quebec hydro (delivering since January 2026) is expected to cover nearly all of the Massachusetts Clean Energy Standard requirement in CY2026.

items.title: Rhode Island aligns its RES Alternative Compliance Payment to $40 flat, adding regional Class I supply
items.summary: Rhode Island's FY2027 budget (enacted June 2026) lowered the state's Renewable Energy Standard Alternative Compliance Payment to $40/MWh flat nominal — down from roughly $87 and no longer indexed to CPI — bringing it in line with Massachusetts and Connecticut, per an Aug 17, 2026 Power Advisory analysis. The change, together with broadened existing-renewable eligibility, effectively increases regional Class I REC supply.

items.title: Acadia Center granted intervenor status in Eversource's Connecticut distribution rate case
items.summary: On August 14, 2026 Acadia Center was granted intervenor status in Eversource's pending PURA rate case, where the utility seeks up to an 18% bill increase (a headline ~$727M once storm costs are included). Acadia is challenging the requested 10.25% return on equity as 'unreasonable and out of step with ROEs nationwide' and is pushing for performance-based ratemaking; new rates would take effect July 1, 2027.

items.title: Rhode Island Energy's winter Last Resort Service rate set at 17.029¢/kWh, effective Oct 1 (Docket 26-27-EL)
items.summary: Rhode Island Energy filed on July 22–24, 2026 to raise its residential Last Resort Service supply rate to 17.029¢/kWh for the Oct 1, 2026–Mar 31, 2027 winter period — about 15% above last winter's 14.77¢/kWh, roughly $12/month more for a typical 500 kWh home. The rate now runs through March 31, 2027, with the next default-rate reset scheduled for April 1, 2027.

items.title: NH Gov. Ayotte signs SB 538 extending net metering for queued municipal solar
items.summary: SB 538 (Chapter 315, effective Sept 8, 2026) supports municipal solar projects up to 5 MW and guarantees the current net-metering credit for 20 years for cities, towns, school districts and counties whose projects were already in the interconnection queue. It was signed July 10, 2026.
